newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies close higher ahead of CME data.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies close higher ahead of CME data.

text.p: CME pork belly futures held much of late morning gain to close stronger ahead of Tuesday's weekly CME out-of-town report, with technicals adding to the runup from early lows, traders said.

Pork bellies surged from morning lows on short covering that developed when futures held technical support. Expectations for a small in-movement last week at out-of-town warehouses also provided suppot, they said.
Futures closed 1.225 to 0.275 cent a lb higher with February up 0.975 at 77.875 cents after holding technical support at 76.375 cents, basis February.

The market appeared oversold and started to rally on local short covering. Expectations by pit traders that the out-of-town report would show an in-movement of less than 1.0 million lbs compared with early analysts' estimates for a 1.0- to 2.0-million-lb in movement added to support, they said.
Buying by RBH added to the advance and touched off buy stops. ABN Chicogo Corp bought late to keep prices supported. E.D.&F. Man was an early seller, pit sources said.
After the close, the CME reported a net in-movement of 845,000 lbs which should buoy belly futures again Wednesday, sources said.

Hog futures rallied from early lows when locals actively covered early short sales. A large buy order at 76.800 cents, basis Febraury, from Rand Financials put a floor in the market and prices turned up along with pork bellies, traders said.

Hogs had ranged mixed early as concern over another weather front prompted support while current heavy marketings of hogs from the last weather front kept a lid on prices. Cash hogs are called steady to lower for Wednesday on the recent stepped up marketings, they said.
Rand bought on the advance while Cargill Investor Services spread long April/short February, pit sources said.
In hog options, LIT division of First Options bought April 75 puts and sold 72 puts on a one for two basis early. E.D.&F. Man sold February 78 calls before the rally in futures, pit sources added.
Hog futures closed 0.600 cent per lb higher to 0.200 lower with February up most at 77.725 cents.
